gen-luckiest-guy-manrope: Luckiest Guy hits with a high, mean line and ink that looks poured at a single width, loud and cheerful. Then Manrope settles in as a friendly sans, its curves left wide open and its capitals barely taller than the lowercase.
gen-mystery-quest-satoshi: Nostalgic and a bit bookish, Mystery Quest keeps its curved strokes open and its ascenders compact above tall lowercase. Satoshi is the lighter hand, a plain sans with a soaring x-height and a technical pen's single line weight.
gen-press-start-2p-switzer: Press Start 2P spaces its letters like cut-outs pinned far apart. That look earns its keep when the words are big and brief, while Switzer stays out of the way with wire-like, tubular sans-serif letterforms and a tall waist line.
gen-audiowide-gf-cascadia-code: Futuristic and tile-like, Audiowide sets its glyphs apart with wide grout lines and tall lowercase. Cascadia Code follows with a wire-thin monoline skeleton, and its generous spacing means you can trim its size without losing clarity.
gen-audiowide-gf-cascadia-mono: Futuristic through and through, Audiowide has tall lowercase and tile-like glyphs. Cascadia Mono counters with a compact plain sans skyline, curves as thick as its stems, and letters standing like pins in a wide board.
gen-righteous-work-sans: Contemporary and approachable, the body text here has c tips that never creep toward touching and a high mean line. Work Sans quietly backs up Righteous, whose bowls fill the line like thin steel rod bent into shape.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-fs-asap: Playful and commanding, Early GameBoy stretches its tracking wide and shows a modest thick-thin difference under a skyward x-height line. Asap stays low-key beside it as a plain sans with open arcs.
gen-tourney-fs-supreme: Bold and athletic, Tourney cuts every stroke to one width, stretches its words wide, and puffs up its small letters. Supreme looks crisp beside it as a plain sans, so a modest size works well.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-fs-asap: Adventurous and wide-striding, Eight Bit Dragon spaces its towering lowercase far apart with a small stroke shift. Asap does the quiet work, a sans with open arcs and lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans brings tall, sturdy lowercase and an e whose eye opens clearly to the right. Edo SZ answers with cast-iron-tall lowercase in a single constant stroke width, so a bigger size suits it.
